name: Morocco

income_tax.summary: Resident individuals pay income tax (IR) on worldwide income on a six-band scale from 0% to 37% (0% to MAD 40,000; 37% above MAD 180,000). Employee social security is 4.48% on pay up to MAD 6,000 a month plus 2.26% mandatory health (AMO) with no ceiling. Independents in the single professional contribution (CPU) regime pay 1.5% of turnover.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Self-employed in the CPU regime pay a flat 1.5% of turnover covering AMO, pension and family allowances (Wafir, secondary). Independents outside CPU fall under the TNS regime; rates not found.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No local income surtax found. Personal allowance of MAD 35,000 is the salaried professional-expense deduction: capped at MAD 35,000 (PwC: 25% rate above MAD 78,000 gross), which is reached at any gross salary above MAD 140,000; it is for employees, not for independents, who deduct actual expenses. Family-charge and mandatory-contribution deductions are not applied. Employee rate shown is AMO 2.26% (uncapped), the marginal rate above the ceiling; an additional 4.48% (CNSS short-term 0.33%, retirement 3.96%, IPE 0.19%) applies to pay up to MAD 6,000 a month (MAD 72,000 a year), about MAD 3,226 a year at most (Wafir).

sources.title: Morocco - Individual - Taxes on personal income (last reviewed 30 Apr 2026)
Morocco - Individual - Other taxes (last reviewed 30 Apr 2026)

open_questions: Family-charge deductions and deductibility of mandatory CNSS/AMO contributions are not applied (persona is single).
TNS (non-CPU) self-employed contribution rates not found; CPU 1.5% of turnover comes from Wafir only.
The 4.48% capped contribution is not representable in the single-rate field.
PwC page reviewed 30 April 2026 does not state the scale's effective year.

Deductibility of the AMO health contribution (the recorded 2.26%) and CNSS contributions could not be established: the opened PwC deductions page addresses only pension insurance contributions (capped at 50% of net taxable salary).

residence_routes: EU, US and other citizens: non-Moroccans need a residence card (carte de sejour) to settle; skilled employees generally need a work contract approved by the labour authorities and a Moroccan employer. No Moroccan digital-nomad visa was found. Casablanca Finance City offers a company regime but no personal tax relief (existing jurisdiction file).
open_questions: No digital-nomad visa found; not confirmed from an official source.
Work contract approval (ANAPEC) and residence card process not researched.
